item.description: By Ndahi Marama, Maiduguri The African Democratic Congress (ADC) in Borno State and former Commissioner for Home Affairs, Information and Culture, Inuwa Bwala, have traded accusations over claims about Governor Babagana Zulum’s treatment of opposition parties in the state. The dispute followed a Facebook post by Bwala defending Zulum’s record on political tolerance, which the ADC described as a distortion of the situation on the ground. In a statement issued on Thursday, the ADC State Publicity Secretary, Baba Ahmed Mustapha, challenged Bwala’s position, citing the demolition of a property belonging to opposition figure Atom Magira, alleged threats against opposition supporters, the detention of youths who displayed “Tinubu Must Go” placards, and claims that the party had faced restrictions on campaign venues and billboards. But Bwala dismissed the ADC’s response, questioning Mustapha’s experience in public communication and describing the party’s statement as an attempt to misrepresent his earlier analysis. The council was reacting to Kwankwaso’s call for Atiku to step down for Peter Obi, describing the intervention as self-serving and an attempt to distract opposition parties from the task of dislodging the ruling All Progressives Congress, APC, amid mounting hardship, hunger, poverty and insecurity. item.title: FRC operated without board for over 13 years, nominee tells senate
item.description: By Henry Umoru ABUJA — President Bola Tinubu’s nominee for chairman of the board of the Fiscal Responsibility Commission (FRC), Abdullahi Saidu, has told the Senate that the commission has operated without a board for more than 13 years, a situation he said has hindered its operations. Saidu spoke on Wednesday when he appeared before the Senate Committee on Finance for screening alongside six other nominees. He said the absence of a board had left the commission with significant institutional challenges, adding that the incoming board would have to rebuild its operations if confirmed. Saidu said the commission was expected to establish offices in at least one location in each of the six geopolitical zones but currently operated only from Abuja. He pledged to work with the National Assembly and other stakeholders to strengthen the commission and improve its capacity to discharge its mandate. The nominee also disclosed that the commission lacked prosecutorial powers, explaining that it could investigate cases and forward its findings to the Attorney-General of the Federation and Minister of Justice for prosecution. He said the proposed board would seek a review of the law establishing the commission to strengthen its independence and operational capacity. Saidu further pledged to improve government revenue by strengthening the monitoring of operating surpluses generated by government-owned and other organisations covered by the commission’s mandate. According to him, some revenue-generating organisations fail to remit the appropriate share of their operating surpluses to the Federal Government. He said such organisations were expected to remit 80 per cent of their operating surpluses to the Consolidated Revenue Fund while retaining 20 per cent for their operations. “Because the commission is not informed, so they just declare whatever they feel they want to declare,” he said. Saidu assured the committee that, if confirmed, the board would strengthen monitoring to ensure that the appropriate revenues were declared and remitted. He expressed confidence that the commission’s performance could improve within a year, provided it received the necessary support from the National Assembly and other stakeholders. The screening was presided over by Senator Lere Oyewumi, vice-chairman of the committee, who represented its chairman, Senator Sani Musa. Addressing the nominees, Oyewumi said managing the commission required specialised knowledge and preparation, noting that the assignment differed from other public service roles. Senator Osita Ngwu, representing Enugu West, moved a motion for Saidu and the other nominees to take a bow and leave, while Senator Sadiq Suleiman Umar, representing Kwara North, seconded the motion. item.title: NSIB Probes Mid-Air Door Separation On Aircraft En Route To Lagos
item.description: The Nigerian Safety Investigation Bureau (NSIB) says it has launched an investigation into the separation of an aircraft door involving a Challenger 604 operated by Triton. In a statement, the Bureau said the aircraft, with registration number T7-SEI, was flying from Abuja to Lagos when its crew declared a mayday after the door separated at an altitude of 3,500 feet. The aircraft subsequently returned to Abuja and landed safely on Runway 22. All nine persons on board, comprising three crew members and six passengers, were accounted for. The NSIB said the separated door had been recovered and secured as investigators began work to determine the circumstances surrounding the incident. The Bureau said further updates would be provided as the investigation progresses. The post NSIB Probes Mid-Air Door Separation On Aircraft En Route To Lagos appeared first on Channels Television .

item.title: Kenya Records Third Ebola Case, Health Ministry Says
item.description: Kenya has recorded its third case of Ebola, a close relative of the country’s first two Ebola cases, the health ministry said on Friday. The country had not reported a single case of the contagious virus until last week, after a Kenyan man who had been living in the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) died after returning to Kenya. Just over a week later, a second man, a relative of the first, also tested positive for the virus while in quarantine. The DRC declared its 17th Ebola outbreak in May. The deadly disease has killed more than 15,000 people in Africa over the past 50 years. The 65-year-old woman was a “primary contact and a close relative of the first and second cases”, the ministry said in a statement, adding that she had been in quarantine since October 6. A Kenyan Ministry of Health official checks the temperature of a traveller at the Busia One Stop Border Post (OSBP) on the Kenya-Uganda border as health authorities step up Ebola screening measures, in Busia on October 12, 2026. Photo by BRIGHT EMOJA / AFP After developing symptoms, including “fever, sore throat and malaise”, she was isolated and tested positive for the virus. The ministry emphasised that the risk to the public “remains low” and there was “no evidence of community transmission”. It said of 130 contacts, 127 had been traced and were in quarantine, with efforts “ongoing to trace and quarantine the three remaining contacts”. On Wednesday, the ministry confirmed its second case, a 39-year-old relative of the first victim, stating he was in isolation and there was “no evidence” of any large-scale transmission of the virus. The country has never previously reported a case. Neighbouring Uganda recorded 20 people infected, almost all of whom had travelled from the neighbouring DRC, and two deaths, before being declared Ebola-free in August. Kenya’s first victim was a national, who has not been named but was referred to as a 40-year-old businessman. He fell ill around a month ago and had been treated in the DRC, before travelling overland to the Ugandan capital, Kampala, and flying into Nairobi on October 3. He was hospitalised in Nairobi but died on October 5, according to Health Minister Aden Duale. According to Congolese health authorities, the outbreak has infected 9,066 people so far and caused 4,381 deaths since the emergence in the DRC of the Bundibugyo strain of the Ebola virus, for which there is still neither a vaccine nor a specific treatment. item.title: Real Madrid demand La Liga chief’s resignation
item.description: By Adegboyega Adeleye Real Madrid have demanded the immediate resignation of La Liga president Javier Tebas after he compared the club’s criticism of referees and its use of Real Madrid TV to propaganda techniques associated with Nazi official Joseph Goebbels. According to the BBC, Tebas made the remarks in a post on X, accusing Real Madrid’s management of directing media criticism of referees and repeatedly promoting claims that the club had been wronged. The club called his comparison “deeply offensive” and “morally repugnant”. Tebas wrote that Real Madrid’s management “directs an orchestra of mouthpieces” and that its television channel “leads the singing”. He said the club’s approach was to “select the plays that suit them, repeat the grievance, feed the suspicion, and point fingers at the enemies”. He added: “That method recalls propaganda mechanisms exploited by Goebbels, Nazi Germany’s minister of propaganda: systematic repetition, construction of an enemy, and subordination of facts to the narrative.” Tebas later said his comparison was with “those propaganda techniques” and “not with an ideology”. Real Madrid rejected that clarification, saying it did not lessen what the club called the “institutionally unworthy nature” of his statements. In its response, Real Madrid said: “It is absolutely intolerable and extraordinarily serious that someone holding two positions of utmost responsibility in Spanish football resorts to a comparison with the propaganda methods of the Nazi regime to discredit our club, its management and its television.” The club demanded Tebas resign both as La Liga president and as vice-president of the Spanish Football Association. It described the remarks as another episode in what it called his repeated attacks on Real Madrid, its president and its media outlets. Tebas and Real Madrid president Florentino Pérez have clashed before, including over the club’s support for the proposed European Super League and its complaints about refereeing. item.title: Why Sporting Rivalries Matter in Creating Sport’s Greatest Stories
item.description: Sport is a means of entertainment for millions of people across the globe. It is full of memorable moments and actions that make it worthwhile. However, some moments stay with people for much longer than others. A last-minute goal, a record-breaking performance or a dramatic comeback can become part of sporting history. item.description: Rivers State Governor, Siminalayi Fubara, has awarded ₦50 million to players and coaches of the state-sponsored Real Madrid Academy following their participation in an international football tour of Southampton, United Kingdom. Governor Fubara announced the reward when the academy’s management, officials and players visited him at Government House in Port Harcourt to present a trophy they won during the tour. The delegation comprised 60 students and 12 staff members who participated in the international football engagement, providing the young players with an opportunity to develop their skills, gain international exposure and experience football beyond their immediate environment.
